title: Intel (INTC) Stock Q2 2026 Earnings Preview: What to Expect
description: Intel is set to announce its Q2 2026 earnings after market close on July 23, 2026, with analysts expecting modest profitability and revenue growth. Consensus .

faq.q: What is non-GAAP EPS and why is it important?
faq.a: Non-GAAP EPS (Earnings Per Share) is a measure of a company's profitability that excludes certain non-recurring or non-cash expenses, such as stock-based compensation, restructuring charges, or acquisition-related costs. It is important because it often provides a clearer picture of a company's core operational performance, as it strips out items that may distort the underlying business trend.

faq.q: How does Intel Foundry contribute to Intel's strategy?
faq.a: Intel Foundry is a crucial part of Intel's IDM 2.0 strategy, aiming to become a major provider of chip manufacturing services for external customers, similar to TSMC. This diversification is intended to leverage Intel's manufacturing capabilities, enhance its technological leadership, and create a new revenue stream.

faq.q: What are "AI PCs" and why are they relevant to Intel?
faq.a: AI PCs are personal computers equipped with specialised hardware, like Neural Processing Units (NPUs), designed to efficiently handle AI workloads directly on the device, rather than relying solely on cloud-based AI. Intel is pushing for the adoption of AI PCs as it drives demand for its client CPUs, integrating AI capabilities into its Core Series processors.

faq.q: What is the significance of gross margin in Intel's earnings?
faq.a: Gross margin (revenue minus cost of goods sold, divided by revenue) indicates how efficiently a company produces its goods. For Intel, it's a key indicator of manufacturing efficiency, pricing power, and the cost of ramping up new, advanced process nodes. A higher gross margin generally implies better profitability from core operations.

faq.q: How do analyst estimates influence stock performance?
faq.a: Analyst estimates set the "bar" for a company's performance. If a company reports results that "beat" these estimates, its stock often rises, as it signals stronger-than-expected business health. Conversely, a "miss" can lead to a stock decline. The magnitude of the beat or miss, along with management's future guidance, heavily influences market reaction.
